_about: Hit zone slot NAMES, dictated by Raven on review -- one monster at a time, reading each row's capsules on the render (a row's name draws its rBodyData shapes, see pickZone in index.html). The ROM ships no zone-name table, so a person saying what a slot is is the only source there is. Keyed by monster id, then by damage-table slot (the row index hitzones.json's tables and capsules use). These are the only slot names the chart shows (since 2026-09-16 hitzones.json's community names are not shown); a slot not named here reads Slot N. `reviewed` is the date the names were given. A monster's `hide` maps a slot to the reason the chart leaves that row out (Raven's call, one slot at a time); deleting the key lists the row again. A monster's `objects` maps a slot to why its shapes sit on a thing the monster holds rather than on its body: build-hitzones.py leaves those capsules out of the vertex bake, so no part of the body takes that row's colour. Deleting the key bakes them into the body again.

What reads them instead is not found (a scan for tests of bit 8 on +0xa/+0xb found none). _aboutParts: A monster's `parts` names the rows of the chart's Extracts table -- the .dtt PART records, a different list from the damage slots (a limb the damage table keeps as one row can be two records, left and right). Keyed by part-record index; a record not named here reads Part N. First filled 2026-09-17 from `slots` by build/hitzone-states/extract_names.py, using the capsules' own slot and part-record fields (bdd record+6 and +8) and, where a slot is shared by two records, which side of the model each one's capsules sit on (Raven's Left/Right slot names say which side is Left). Raven, 2026-09-17: "Extracts has its own slots, I have noticed some tend to be induvial limbs that were grouped together in the Hit Zones tables", "I will be manually reviewing each monster, I just figured you could fill in some of them easily". `partsFrom` marks a monster whose part names have not been reviewed yet.
